title: California Insurance Code Section 666 (obtaining the reason for cancellation in writing)
claims: Section 666 provides that where the reason for cancellation does not accompany or is not included in the notice of cancellation, the insurer shall, upon written request of the named insured mailed or delivered to the insurer not less than 15 days prior to the effective date of cancellation, specify in writing the reason for the cancellation.
Section 666 requires that the reason be mailed or delivered to the named insured within five days after receipt of the request.

Section 666 provides that, notwithstanding Section 1633.3 of the Civil Code, the writing specifying the reason for cancellation may not be delivered electronically to the insured unless the insured electronically delivered the request to the insurer.
updateCadence: Amended only by legislation. Amended by Stats. 2009, Ch. 433, Sec. 9 (AB 328), effective January 1, 2010.
notes: Read on its own this section speaks only of cancellation, and that is how its text is written. It reaches nonrenewal by cross-reference rather than by its own terms: section 663(a) requires a written notice of nonrenewal to include the statement required by this section, so the same mechanism for getting a reason in writing attaches to a policy that is not renewed. The section is a right to ask rather than a right to be told unprompted, and the request carries its own deadline, not less than 15 days before the effective date of cancellation, which falls inside the 20-day notice period section 662 provides. A reader who waits for an explanation to arrive can lose the request window while waiting.
